_about: Public-domain E. B. Pusey (1800-1882, Regius Professor of Hebrew at Oxford, a leader of the Oxford Movement) for the Word Hoard: The Minor Prophets with a commentary (Oxford: Parker, catalogued 1860), Daniel the Prophet (1868) and Lenten Sermons (1874), raw Internet Archive OCR. Added 2026-10-03 by lane A, round 10 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. No uids minted. Filled out 2026-11-15 from the Oxford Movement Historical Theology Collection on Adam's Libronix list ('Libronix authors - reconciled.md', add-on OXF). Pusey's five OXF titles, plus the Eirenicon of 1865 (its first part).

pusey-minor-prophets-1860: The Minor Prophets, with a Commentary Explanatory and Practical (Oxford: J. H. and J. Parker; catalogued 1860)
pusey-daniel-1868: Daniel the Prophet: Nine Lectures Delivered in the Divinity School of the University of Oxford (Oxford: J. Parker, 1868)
pusey-lenten-sermons-1874: Lenten Sermons, Preached Chiefly to Young Men at the Universities (Oxford: J. Parker, 1874)
pusey-letter-bishop-oxford-1839: A Letter to Richard, Lord Bishop of Oxford, on the Tendency to Romanism (Oxford: J. H. Parker, 1839)
pusey-letter-archbishop-1842: A Letter to His Grace the Archbishop of Canterbury, on Some Circumstances Connected with the Present Crisis in the English Church (Oxford: J. H. Parker, 1842)
pusey-real-presence-fathers-1855: The Doctrine of the Real Presence, as Contained in the Fathers (Oxford: J. H. Parker, 1855)
pusey-councils-1857: The Councils of the Church, from the Council of Jerusalem, A.D. 51, to the Council of Constantinople, A.D. 381 (Oxford: J. H. Parker, 1857)
pusey-eirenicon-1865: An Eirenicon, in a Letter to the Author of 'The Christian Year' (Oxford: J. H. and J. Parker, 1865)
pusey-first-letter-newman-1869: First Letter to the Very Rev. J. H. Newman, D.D., in Explanation Chiefly in Regard to the Reverential Love Due to the Ever-Blessed Theotokos (Oxford: J. Parker, 1869)
pusey-notes-questions-brinckman-1891: Notes and Questions on the Catholic Faith and Religion, the notes and answers compiled chiefly from the works and in the words of Dr. Pusey [by Arthur Brinckman], preface by T. T. Carter (London: A. D. Innes, 1891)
